features: HEADS UP — FIGURES WILL CHANGE: the amount spent on a budget item now includes IMMEDIATE SETTLEMENTS, which were previously invisible to the budget. Items that looked untouched may now show as partly committed or over budget: this is not a new error, it is spending that was already there and simply wasn't counted. No database migration.

HEADS UP — FIGURES WILL CHANGE: the "Budget" total at the top of the Chart of Accounts no longer inflates with overspending. It used to add up amounts already raised to actual cost, so it grew alongside expenses and stopped being a budget: it now stays the approved figure.

HEADS UP — FIGURES WILL CHANGE: in the Chart of Accounts, charges billed to individual units no longer add to an item's shared spending. This was the only page counting them, disagreeing with the Dashboard and Instalment Plans.

New "Actual" column beside Budget in the accounts list: for each item you can read what was planned and what was actually spent, with over-budget items highlighted in red and the excess shown on hover.
New "Actual" total at the top of the list, next to Budget and Unforeseen: the overall spending of the chart of accounts, which previously could not be read anywhere on that page.

Clicking an item's actual amount opens the list of movements behind it — recorded invoices and immediate settlements, with date, description, type and amount — and from there you reach the individual entry in the General Ledger. Reversals appear as negative amounts, because they are part of the story that explains the total.

The accounts list can now be sorted by CODE as well as by name, using a selector above the list. Sorting is natural (A.2 comes before A.10, 999 before 1020) and items without a code are grouped at the end instead of scattering through the list. The choice is remembered, and the "Expense breakdown" printout follows it, so the PDF matches what you see on screen. Requested by an administrator.

The "Coverage" label in the Chart of Accounts is now "Covered by instalment plan", and a line under the bar clarifies that it shows the share of budget already included in a plan issued to unit owners — not the money actually spent. These are two different things and were being confused.

On the Supplier Invoices page a notice reports how many immediate settlements exist in the financial year and links to them, pre-filtered, in the General Ledger: they are created from a button on this page but never appear here, because they do not produce an invoice. The notice can be dismissed and returns after six months.

New "Record payment" action in each invoice menu: it opens the payment form with supplier, IBAN and the invoice already selected with its amount. It only appears on invoices that can actually be paid — one awaiting assembly ratification, pending approval or disputed cannot be, and the action previously led to a dead end.

From an overspend card you can jump straight to creating the instalment plan, with the management period and type (ordinary or extraordinary) already set. The link only appears when the chosen strategy is a supplementary instalment: with reserve-fund coverage or year-end settlement, an instalment is not the answer.
The "Requires instalments" label on overspends is now "To be covered by supplementary instalment", and every recovery strategy has its own explicit label.

Fixed: the "Back" button in the accounting entry detail and in a unit owner's statement never returned to the page you came from. It read a value the framework does not provide, so it always fell back to the default register, no matter where you arrived from.
Fixed: the "Record payment" action already existed in the code but was disabled because it pointed to a non-existent address; enabling it as it was would have produced an error.

Fixed: two tests in the suite failed intermittently due to a collision in automatically generated random data; a third issue of the same kind made it impossible to write tests involving two buildings at once — precisely the ones that verify isolation between buildings.
Fixed: the Chart of Accounts page could not be checked by automated tests because one query used syntax valid only on MySQL. It is now covered, including the header totals.

Interface refinements: the "Expected reference number" field aligned with the others in the immediate settlement form, the "Allocation locked" notice moved inside the section it describes, the accounts list header reorganised onto two lines, percentages and amounts with correct separators.
